ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Consider a uniform isosceles triangle prism $\mathrm{ABC}$, with the apex angle $\theta=110^{\circ}$ at vertex $\mathrm{A}$. One of the sides, $\mathrm{AC}$, is coated with silver, allowing it to function as a mirror. When a monochrome light-ray of wavelength $\lambda$ approaches side $\mathrm{AB}$ at an angle of incidence $\alpha$, it first refracts, then reaches side AC, reflects, and continues to base BC. After another refraction, the ray eventually exits the prism at the angle of emergence which is also equal to the angle of incidence (see Fig. A).
<image_1>

What is the relative refractive index of the prism for that particular wavelength $\lambda$ with respect to the outside environment, given that $\alpha=70^{\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the attached figure, Fig. A is a light-blue isosceles triangular prism, with the vertex labeled A, the endpoints of the base labeled C and B, and θ marked at the vertex angle. A red light ray is incident from the right side onto side AB, enters the prism and then reaches the left side AC. AC is a silvered reflecting surface. After the light ray is reflected at AC, it reaches the base BC and is refracted out from BC. In the figure, arcs beside the red dashed normals mark the angle of incidence and the angle of emergence α, indicating that these angles are measured relative to the normal to the interface. Reasoning: The vertex angle θ = 110°, and the prism is an isosceles triangle, so the two base angles are β = (180° - 110°)/2 = 35°. Let the angle of refraction after the light ray is refracted into the prism at face AB be r. From Snell's law at face AB, if the relative refractive index of the outside medium is taken as 1 and the refractive index of the prism relative to the outside is n, then sin α = n sin r. When the light ray emerges at face BC, the angle of emergence is equal to the angle of incidence α, so at face BC there is n sin i = sin α, where i is the angle of incidence inside the prism when the light ray reaches BC. Comparing the two equations gives sin i = sin r; taking the angles in the figure to all be acute-angle cases, obtain i = r. Directly tracking the angles according to the light path in Fig. A, and considering the reflection at face AC, the internal angle of incidence upon reaching BC satisfies i = 180° - 3β - r. Substituting β = 35°, obtain i = 180° - 105° - r = 75° - r. Also i = r, so r = 75° - r, namely r = 37.5°. Therefore n = sin 70° / sin 37.5° ≈ 1.5436.

It refracts into the prism, reflects from side $\mathrm{AC}$, then reaches base $\mathrm{BC}$. method.method_draft: Use direct angle chasing in Fig. A. From the image, identify the triangular prism ABC with ray entering face AB, reflecting from silvered face AC, and exiting through base BC; the red dashed arcs indicate the incidence and emergence angles are measured from the surface normals. From the text, take the apex angle theta = 110° and alpha = 70°. Since the prism is isosceles, each base angle is beta = (180° - 110°)/2 = 35°. Let r be the refracted angle inside the prism at AB. Snell's law at AB gives sin(alpha) = n sin(r). At BC, the emergent angle equals alpha, so Snell's law gives n sin(i) = sin(alpha), hence i = r for the internal incidence angle i at BC. Now use the ray geometry plus reflection at AC: tracing the internal ray directions relative to the side normals gives i = 180° - 3 beta - r = 75° - r. Therefore r = 75° - r, so r = 37.5°. Substitute into n = sin(70°)/sin(37.5°) to obtain n ≈ 1.5436.

method.method_draft: Use an unfolded-mirror construction. From Fig. A, note that the ray reflects once from AC before reaching BC. Replace the reflection at AC by reflecting the lower/output part of the prism across AC, so the internally reflected ray becomes one straight line in an unfolded diagram. From the text, beta = (180° - theta)/2 = 35° and alpha = 70°. Let r be the internal refracted angle at AB. Because the incident and emergent outside angles are both alpha, Snell's law at AB and at BC implies that the internal angle to the normal at AB and the internal angle to the normal of the reflected image of BC are equal, both r. In the unfolded geometry, compute the angle between the inward normal to AB and the reflected normal to BC: with base angle beta = 35°, this angle is 180° - 3 beta = 75°. The straight ray bisects this 75° angle because it makes equal angle r with both normals, so 2r = 75° and r = 37.5°. Then n = sin(70°)/sin(37.5°) ≈ 1.5436.

After the light ray is reflected at AC, it reaches the base BC and is refracted out from BC. In the figure, arcs beside the red dashed normals mark the angle of incidence and the angle of emergence α, indicating that these angles are measured relative to the normal to the interface.

Reasoning: The vertex angle θ = 110°, and the prism is an isosceles triangle, so the two base angles are β = (180° - 110°)/2 = 35°. Let the angle of refraction after the light ray is refracted into the prism at face AB be r. From Snell's law at face AB, if the relative refractive index of the outside medium is taken as 1 and the refractive index of the prism relative to the outside is n, then sin α = n sin r. When the light ray emerges at face BC, the angle of emergence is equal to the angle of incidence α, so at face BC there is n sin i = sin α, where i is the angle of incidence inside the prism when the light ray reaches BC. Comparing the two equations gives sin i = sin r; taking the angles in the figure to all be acute-angle cases, obtain i = r.

Directly tracking the angles according to the light path in Fig. A, and considering the reflection at face AC, the internal angle of incidence upon reaching BC satisfies i = 180° - 3β - r. Substituting β = 35°, obtain i = 180° - 105° - r = 75° - r. Also i = r, so r = 75° - r, namely r = 37.5°.

Therefore n = sin 70° / sin 37.5° ≈ 1.5436.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Consider a uniform isosceles triangular prism $\mathrm{ABC}$, with apex angle $\theta=110^{\circ}$ at vertex $\mathrm{A}$. One side, $\mathrm{AC}$, is silvered so that it acts as a mirror. A monochromatic light ray of wavelength $\lambda$ is incident on side $\mathrm{AB}$ at angle $\alpha$. It refracts into the prism, reflects from side $\mathrm{AC}$, then reaches base $\mathrm{BC}$. After refraction at $\mathrm{BC}$, the ray emerges with angle of emergence equal to the angle of incidence (see Fig. A). What is the relative refractive index of the prism for wavelength $\lambda$ with respect to the outside medium, given that $\alpha=70^{\circ}$?

What is the relative refractive index of the prism for wavelength $\lambda$ with respect to the outside medium, given that $\alpha=70^{\circ}$?
